Friend—perhaps he could stress this to his constituents—that the clinical risk of contracting Ebola from sitting next to someone who is not exhibiting feverish symptoms is very low.
I hope that will reassure his constituents.
I want to stress to my hon.
One of the lessons we learned in the Christmas period is that we do not want people to have to wait as long.
That is why the clinical advice was, and remains, that it is perfectly safe for someone to travel on a train if they are not displaying the symptoms.

That is why we have said that if people in the high-risk categories—those who have had contact with Ebola patients—say they are unwell, we will have a different protocol going forward even if their temperature is within the normal range.
We recognise that we do not know everything about this disease and therefore want to be precautionary.
We want to go further, however.
We have learned the lessons to speed up the process so that people, I trust, will not have to wait as long.
